audit.why: Lane difficulty is stated as HARD / 7-10 with Gnar taking 4 of 7 stages, which matches the 44.88% Emerald+ win rate over 205 games. Early is a Chomp-bully window for Trundle; mid onward is a kite lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Power spikes are named but carry no timings. GNAR! is described as 'the long transform cooldown' without a number, so the reader cannot tell how long the punish window actually is.
audit.why: GNAR! (R) is 90/60/30s per Riot Data Dragon. Rank 1 is a 90-second window in which Mega form's kill threat is simply gone — that is the single most actionable number in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Stated 90/60/30s in breakdown.cooldowns and 90s at rank 1 in content mid and spikes[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability-name errors and one decisive interaction absent. 'Hyper passive' is used twice for what is actually Hyper (W); Gnar's real passive is Rage Gene. More importantly, nothing anywhere says that Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain, which is exactly the wall GNAR! (R) needs to convert its knockback into a stun.
audit.why: Riot text: Pillar of Ice 'becoming impassable terrain'; GNAR! 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage'. Both kit files carry the terrain flag. A Trundle who drops E behind himself against Mega Gnar builds his own execution wall.
audit.corrected: Named Boomerang Throw (Q), Hyper (W) and Rage Gene (P) correctly, and stated that your own Pillar of Ice counts as a wall for GNAR!.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block repeats 'track it' without any duration for either GNAR! or Boomerang Throw.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s but refunds part of that if Gnar catches the return — the poke rhythm is set by whether he catches it, not by the raw number.
audit.corrected: Added the 90/60/30 GNAR! numbers and the catch-refund note to wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is twice credited with an attack-speed steal or 'attack-speed debuff' (wants.you[0], spikes[3].text). It has neither.
audit.why: Riot text for Chomp: 'dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage.' The attack speed in this matchup belongs to Frozen Domain and is yours, not something taken off Gnar.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the AD drain plus Chomp's own slow, and credited the attack speed to your W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json Q Chomp, W Frozen Domain

audit.whatIsWrong: Text says to 'use Pillar of Ice defensively to interrupt his Hop approach'. Pillar does not interrupt a leap already in flight.
audit.why: Hop is a leap to a location; terrain denies the path and the landing options around it, but nothing in Riot's text supports interrupting the leap mid-air.
audit.corrected: Reworded to placing Pillar on his landing spot / cutting the follow-up path rather than 'interrupting' the Hop.

edits.before: Mini-Gnar's boomerang (Q) and Hyper passive autos out-range Chomp from level 1 — you have no Frozen Domain yet and cannot win a trade he initiates from distance.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hyper (W) autos out-range Chomp's 300 units from level 1 — with no Frozen Domain yet you cannot win a trade he opens from distance.

edits.before: His ranged form lets him stack Hyper passive without entering your W zone, so every level-2 trade he takes is on his terms before your W ice patch answers his kite.
edits.after: His ranged form banks Rage Gene (P) without ever entering your W zone, so every level-2 trade is on his terms before Frozen Domain's move speed answers his kite.

edits.before: Mega-Gnar at level 6 with GNAR! stun into terrain is the deadliest window in the lane — your Subjugate arrives simultaneously but he controls when he transforms, so he picks the all-in timing.
edits.after: Mega-Gnar at level 6 with GNAR! into terrain is the deadliest window in the lane — Subjugate arrives at the same level, but he owns the Rage bar, so he picks when the all-in happens.

edits.before: Mega-Gnar's GNAR! stun into his team or terrain is his hardest all-in window — Frozen Domain and Pillar together are your only answer if he corners you against a wall.
edits.after: GNAR! is up every 90s at rank 1 and stuns anything it throws into a wall — your own Pillar of Ice is a wall, so never leave ice behind you while Mega form is live.

edits.before: Use Pillar of Ice to cut off his Hop escape and pin him inside your W zone for extended Chomp stacking
edits.after: Pillar of Ice is real terrain — drop it on his Hop landing spot to strand him in your W zone for Chomp stacking

edits.before: Poke with mini-Gnar's boomerang (Q) and Hyper passive procs before you can reach him with Frozen Domain
edits.after: Poke with Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hyper (W), catching the return arc to cut the 16s cooldown down again

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the most dangerous window before your ultimate arrives. Gnar will stack Rage deliberately by auto-attacking you or caster minions and then transform at full bar while you have no Subjugate to punish him. Mega-Gnar's GNAR! into any nearby wall is a stun-chain that kills you if you are at all poke-damaged. Keep your W down as a retreat path, not an aggression tool, and use Pillar of Ice defensively to interrupt his Hop approach rather than offensively. At level 6 the equation flips briefly — Subjugate strips his armor and MR the instant he transforms, so bait the GNAR! stun into open ground, dodge it with a flash or Pillar side-step, then immediately cast R and stand on W to all-in a draining Mega-Gnar who can no longer one-shot you.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the most dangerous window before your ultimate arrives. Gnar banks Rage Gene deliberately by auto-attacking you or caster minions, then transforms at full bar while you have no Subjugate to punish him. Mega GNAR! into any nearby wall is a stun-chain that kills you if you are at all poke-damaged, and Wallop (Mega W) stuns on its own. Keep Frozen Domain down as a retreat path, not an aggression tool, and place Pillar of Ice on his Hop landing spot — never behind yourself, because it is impassable terrain and GNAR! stuns you against it. At level 6 the equation flips: Subjugate strips his armor and MR the instant he transforms, and GNAR! is 90 seconds at rank 1, so bait it into open ground, then cast R and stand on W to all-in a draining Mega-Gnar.

edits.before: Force Frozen Domain trades in melee range so Chomp's AD steal and attack-speed debuff compound before he can hop away
edits.after: Force Frozen Domain trades in melee range so Chomp's AD drain and your own W attack speed compound before he Hops away

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet's Frostfield stacks directly with Chomp's attack-speed steal, making any Mega-Gnar who commits to a fight progressively slower and easier to drain.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's Frostfield layers onto Chomp's own slow and AD drain, making any Mega-Gnar who commits to a fight progressively weaker and easier to run down.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega Stun): matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. Track it before every engage. - Gnar GNAR!: Mega only: knocks up + slows; against a wall it stuns long. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Gnar GNAR! (Mega Stun): matchup-defining — 90/60/30s. His Mega all-in; never fight the transform. - Gnar GNAR!: Mega only: knocks back and slows; anything hitting a wall is stunned, and your Pillar is a wall.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Gnar to deny disengage, or between you and GNAR! (Mega Stun) to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice closes the kit on a 21s cooldown — place it behind Gnar to deny Hop, never behind yourself once Mega is up.
